_about: Nutrient cards on the home screen. Each card is a plain summary of the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements consumer fact sheet linked in source. need = daily amount for ages 19 to 50.

nutrients.food: 1 cup of cooked lentils (daal) gives about 6 mg of iron: most of a man's daily need and a third of a woman's.
nutrients.name: Iron
nutrients.tag: A mineral your blood needs to carry oxygen to every part of your body.
nutrients.does: Iron helps red blood cells carry oxygen around your body. Low iron makes you tired and weak and can lead to anaemia.
nutrients.good: Women with periods need more iron than men. Tea and coffee block iron; vitamin C helps your body absorb it.
nutrients.other: Red meat, chicken liver, fish and eggs.
nutrients.need: Men 8 mg, women 18 mg a day

nutrients.food: One guava gives about 125 mg of vitamin C, more than a whole day's need.
nutrients.name: Vitamin C
nutrients.tag: A vitamin found in fresh fruit that helps wounds heal and helps you absorb iron.
nutrients.does: Vitamin C helps wounds heal, keeps gums and skin healthy, supports the immune system and helps you absorb iron.
nutrients.good: Your body cannot store it, so you need some every day. Long cooking destroys much of it, so fresh fruit is best.
nutrients.other: Potatoes and green chillies also add some.
nutrients.need: Men 90 mg, women 75 mg a day

nutrients.food: Food alone rarely covers it: one egg yolk gives only about 1 mcg (44 IU) of the 15 mcg you need.
nutrients.name: Vitamin D
nutrients.tag: The "sunshine vitamin" your skin makes in sunlight, needed for strong bones.
nutrients.does: Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium, which keeps bones and teeth strong. It also supports muscles.
nutrients.good: Your skin makes vitamin D in sunlight. Very few foods contain it, which is why many people need a supplement.
nutrients.other: Sunlight, egg yolks, fish such as salmon, and fortified milk.

nutrients.food: 1 cup of milk gives about 300 mg of calcium, so 3 cups of milk or yogurt cover most of your day.
nutrients.name: Calcium
nutrients.tag: The main mineral in your bones and teeth, also needed by your muscles and heart.
nutrients.does: Calcium builds strong bones and teeth and helps your muscles, nerves and heart work properly.
nutrients.good: Your body absorbs it best in amounts of 500 mg or less at a time. The calcium in spinach is poorly absorbed.

nutrients.food: 1 cup of milk gives about 1.2 mcg of B12, so 2 cups of milk cover your whole day.
nutrients.name: Vitamin B12
nutrients.tag: A vitamin from animal foods that keeps your nerves and blood cells healthy.
nutrients.does: Vitamin B12 helps make red blood cells and keeps your nerves and brain working well.
nutrients.good: Fruits and vegetables do not contain B12. Vegetarians and older adults are more likely to run low.
fruitsVeg: None: B12 comes only from animal foods
nutrients.other: Meat, fish, eggs, milk and yogurt.

nutrients.food: 1 cup of cooked lentils gives about 360 mcg of folate, almost a whole day's need.
nutrients.name: Folate
nutrients.tag: A B vitamin your body uses to make new cells, very important in pregnancy.
nutrients.does: Folate (folic acid) helps your body make new cells and DNA. It is especially important before and during early pregnancy.
nutrients.good: Folic acid before and in early pregnancy helps prevent birth defects of the baby's brain and spine.
nutrients.need: 400 mcg a day (600 mcg in pregnancy)

nutrients.food: One medium banana gives about 420 mg of potassium; a medium potato with its skin gives about 900 mg.
nutrients.name: Potassium
nutrients.tag: A mineral that keeps your heartbeat steady and your blood pressure healthy.
nutrients.does: Potassium helps your heart beat steadily, your muscles move and keeps blood pressure in a healthy range.
nutrients.good: Most people get enough from food. People with kidney problems should not take potassium supplements without a doctor.
nutrients.need: Men 3,400 mg, women 2,600 mg a day

nutrients.food: Half a cup of raw carrots gives about 460 mcg of vitamin A: about half a man's daily need and two-thirds of a woman's.
nutrients.name: Vitamin A
nutrients.tag: A vitamin that helps you see in dim light and keeps your skin healthy.
nutrients.does: Vitamin A helps you see in dim light and keeps your skin and immune system healthy.
nutrients.good: Too much vitamin A from supplements can be harmful, especially in pregnancy. Food sources are the safest.
nutrients.need: Men 900 mcg, women 700 mcg a day

nutrients.food: A small handful of almonds (about 23, or 28 g) gives 80 mg of magnesium, about a quarter of a woman's daily need.
nutrients.name: Magnesium
nutrients.tag: A mineral that helps your muscles, nerves and heart work and gives you energy.
nutrients.does: Magnesium helps your muscles and nerves work, keeps your heartbeat steady and helps turn food into energy.
nutrients.good: Too much from supplements can cause loose stools. Food sources do not cause this.
nutrients.other: Almonds, cashews, seeds and whole wheat.
nutrients.need: Men 400 mg, women 310 mg a day

nutrients.food: 85 g (3 oz) of cooked beef gives about 5 mg of zinc, roughly half a man's daily need.
nutrients.name: Zinc
nutrients.tag: A mineral that helps your body fight infections and heal wounds.
nutrients.does: Zinc helps your immune system fight germs, helps wounds heal and supports taste and smell.
nutrients.good: Taking a lot of zinc for a long time can lower your copper level. Stay within the safe limit.
nutrients.need: Men 11 mg, women 8 mg a day

nutrients.food: Half a cup of cooked spinach gives about 440 mcg of vitamin K, several days' worth.
nutrients.name: Vitamin K
nutrients.tag: A vitamin from green leafy vegetables that helps your blood clot when you are cut.
nutrients.does: Vitamin K helps your blood clot when you are cut and helps keep bones healthy.
nutrients.good: If you take a blood-thinning medicine, keep the amount of green leafy vegetables steady and talk to your doctor.
nutrients.other: Vegetable oils such as soybean oil.
nutrients.need: Men 120 mcg, women 90 mcg a day

nutrients.food: A small handful of almonds (about 23) gives about 7 mg of vitamin E, almost half your daily need.
nutrients.name: Vitamin E
nutrients.tag: An antioxidant vitamin that protects your cells from damage.
nutrients.does: Vitamin E is an antioxidant: it protects your cells from damage and supports the immune system.
nutrients.good: High-dose vitamin E supplements can increase bleeding risk. Food sources are safe.
nutrients.other: Almonds, sunflower seeds and vegetable oils.

nutrients.name: Vitamin B6
nutrients.tag: A B vitamin that helps your body use protein and keeps your brain and nerves working.
nutrients.does: Vitamin B6 helps your body use protein, make red blood cells and keep your brain and immune system working well.
nutrients.good: Very high doses from supplements taken for a long time can damage nerves, causing numb or tingling hands and feet.
nutrients.food: 1 cup of cooked chickpeas (chanay) gives about 1.1 mg of vitamin B6, almost a whole day's need.

nutrients.name: Niacin (B3)
nutrients.tag: A B vitamin that helps your body turn food into energy.
nutrients.does: Niacin helps turn the food you eat into energy and keeps your skin, nerves and digestion healthy.
nutrients.good: High-dose niacin supplements often cause flushing: red, warm, itchy skin. They can also affect the liver.
nutrients.other: Chicken, fish, peanuts and whole wheat.
nutrients.need: Men 16 mg, women 14 mg a day
nutrients.food: 85 g (3 oz) of cooked chicken breast gives about 10 mg of niacin, around two-thirds of your daily need.

nutrients.name: Omega-3
nutrients.tag: A healthy fat found in fish and nuts that is good for your heart and brain.
nutrients.does: Omega-3 fats are part of every cell in your body and support your heart, brain and eyes.
nutrients.good: Fish gives the omega-3 types (EPA and DHA) your body uses most. Plants give ALA, which your body converts only in small amounts.
nutrients.other: Fish such as salmon, walnuts, flaxseeds and chia seeds.
nutrients.need: Men 1.6 g, women 1.1 g a day (plant omega-3)
nutrients.food: A small handful of walnuts (28 g, about 7 walnuts) gives about 2.5 g of plant omega-3, more than a day's need.

nutrients.name: Iodine
nutrients.tag: A mineral your thyroid gland needs to control your energy and growth.
nutrients.does: Iodine helps your thyroid gland make hormones that control your energy, growth and how your body uses food.
nutrients.good: Too little iodine can cause goitre (a swollen thyroid). Using iodized salt is the easiest way to get enough.
nutrients.other: Iodized salt, fish, milk, yogurt and eggs.
nutrients.need: 150 mcg a day (220 mcg in pregnancy)
nutrients.food: Just a quarter teaspoon of iodized salt gives about 76 mcg of iodine, half your daily need.

nutrients.name: Selenium
nutrients.tag: A mineral that protects your cells and helps your thyroid work.
nutrients.does: Selenium protects your cells from damage, supports your immune system and helps your thyroid work.
nutrients.good: Too much selenium can cause hair and nail loss. A single Brazil nut can hold more than a whole day's amount.
nutrients.other: Fish, eggs, chicken and whole wheat.
nutrients.food: One egg gives about 15 mcg of selenium, over a quarter of your daily need.
